title: Alibi and Portrait
premise: Ulyana Nystrom, a retired detective hiding behind a failing bookshop, is paid in advance by a nervous stranger to prove that a murder has not yet happened — a prediction tied to the upcoming trial of a man convicted years ago of killing Ulyana's late partner. As she investigates, she realizes the 'closed' case everyone swears was settled was itself staged, and that her own memory of that night holds the key. The stranger's prepayment was a trap set by someone who needed Ulyana to reopen the case before the trial collapses. In the end, Ulyana exposes the true killer — the prosecutor who built his career on the lie — and chooses love and found family over the invisible life she built.
about_author: Oscar Iversen is the pen name of a former court clerk who spent a decade transcribing testimony before turning to fiction. He writes quiet mysteries about people who thought they had left their old lives behind.

chapters.title: Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: Ulyana Nystrom, running her failing bookshop, accepts an odd commission: a pale stranger pays triple to prove a murder will not happen. His only clue is a date — the first day of an upcoming trial. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: wary curiosity masking loneliness.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Deaths
chapters.summary: Ulyana reviews the three 'accidents' she quietly solved, establishing her methods and her rule of invisibility. The new client's file contains one name she recognizes: Detective Marek Voss, her late partner. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: grief resurfacing like a tide.

chapters.title: Closed for Good
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: eleven years ago, Voss was found dead in the harbor; a dockworker confessed, and the case closed without Ulyana ever testifying. Present-day Ulyana rereads her own suppressed statement. POV: Ulyana, interwoven with past-tense scenes. Emotional beat: guilt she never named.

chapters.title: The Client Who Vanished
chapters.summary: Ulyana tries to return the money and question her client, but his apartment is empty, lease three days old, furniture rented. Someone manufactured him. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: the chill of realizing she is inside something, not beside it.

chapters.title: Tea with Inspector Halvard
chapters.summary: She cautiously probes her old colleague Inspector Halvard about the trial; he warns her off with genuine warmth and genuine fear. Their tea scene reveals the department still protects the verdict. POV: Halvard briefly, then Ulyana. Emotional beat: loyalty strained against duty.

chapters.title: The Widow's Portrait
chapters.summary: Ulyana visits Voss's widow, Selma, a painter whose portrait of Marek hangs slightly crooked — recently moved. Selma lets slip that someone else asked about the case last month. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: tenderness between two women widowed by the same night.

chapters.title: What the Harbor Keeps
chapters.summary: Ulyana walks the harbor at low tide and finds the physical detail that never fit: the depth of water where Voss drowned couldn't have produced his injuries. She begins rebuilding the night from physics instead of testimony. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: the detective reawakening, hungry and afraid of it.

chapters.title: Found Family, Found Again
chapters.summary: Her makeshift family — teenage shop assistant Priya, retired locksmith Ove, and stray dog Biscuit — notice her slipping back into old habits and stage a small intervention over burnt stew. POV: Priya. Emotional beat: warmth and the fear of losing Ulyana to the case.

chapters.title: The Confession That Was Bought
chapters.summary: Digging into the dockworker's confession, Ulyana finds his defense lawyer was paid through a shell firm connected to then-prosecutor Anders Reinholt — now the judge presiding over the new trial. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: cold clarity hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: A Threat Written in Receipts
chapters.summary: Someone leaves a receipt from her shop on her doorstep dated the night Voss died — proof they know where she was that night. Her alibi, once her shield, becomes a leash. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: invisibility collapsing.

chapters.title: Selma's Second Canvas
chapters.summary: Selma reveals a second, unfinished portrait of Marek painted after his death — from memory of a final phone call he made to her, mentioning 'the ledger.' Ulyana realizes Voss was investigating corruption when he died. POV: Selma. Emotional beat: shared grief becoming alliance.

chapters.title: Ove Picks a Lock He Shouldn't
chapters.summary: Ove helps Ulyana access the archived evidence locker copy of Voss's personal notebook; its pages on 'the ledger' were razored out, but impressions remain. They recover a partial list of names and payments. POV: Ove. Emotional beat: found family choosing risk together.

chapters.title: Halvard's Silence Breaks
chapters.summary: Confronted gently, Halvard admits he suspected the confession was bought but stayed silent to protect his pension and his sick wife. He gives Ulyana one name from the old guard. POV: Halvard. Emotional beat: shame, relief, and the cost of duty.

chapters.title: The Date Explained
chapters.summary: Ulyana deciphers why the client chose the trial's first day: if the conviction is overturned on procedural grounds, the bought confession surfaces automatically. Someone wants the truth out — or wants Ulyana discredited when it does. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: the trap's shape becoming visible.

chapters.title: Priya Follows a Stranger
chapters.summary: Ignoring instructions, Priya tails a man photographing the bookshop and loses him, but photographs his car — registered to a private security firm retained by Reinholt's old office. POV: Priya. Emotional beat: bravery, terror, and pride tangled together.

chapters.title: Night at the Bookshop
chapters.summary: The shop is ransacked; Biscuit is unharmed but shaken, and the intruder left the client's advance money neatly stacked — a message. Ulyana understands: finish the job or be framed for tampering. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into defiance.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't a Client
chapters.summary: Ulyana tracks the fabricated client's paper trail to a grieving brother of the wrongly convicted dockworker, who died in prison. He hired no one — his identity was stolen to bait her. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: fury at how grief gets weaponized.

chapters.title: Reconstructing the Night
chapters.summary: Using the notebook impressions, tide tables, and Selma's phone-call memory, Ulyana reconstructs Voss's death: he met his killer at the harbor voluntarily, and the 'drowning' injuries came first. Only one person fits every detail. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: dread as the picture completes.

chapters.title: What I Saw That Night
chapters.summary: Ulyana finally confronts her own suppressed memory: she saw Reinholt near the harbor that night and buried it, convinced she'd imagined it, because testifying would have destroyed her career before it began. POV: Ulyana, deep interiority. Emotional beat: the novel's thematic heart — memory as both wound and weapon.

chapters.title: Eve of Trial
chapters.summary: With Halvard's reluctant help, Ulyana packages the evidence for the defense and the press, knowing Reinholt will strike first. Selma finishes the second portrait — Marek smiling — as a quiet vigil gathers at the shop. POV: multiple brief POVs. Emotional beat: found family arming themselves with truth.

chapters.title: Alibi and Portrait
chapters.summary: At the courthouse, Reinholt attempts to have the evidence excluded and Ulyana arrested; the finished portrait, showing the watch Reinholt lost at the harbor that night, becomes the corroborating exhibit. Confronted publicly, he breaks. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: climax — love and duty finally pointing the same direction.

chapters.title: Open Sign
chapters.summary: Weeks later: the dockworker posthumously exonerated, the trial proceeding honestly, Ulyana's role quietly credited. She flips the shop's sign to OPEN, keeps the client's payment framed as a joke, and lets her found family stay for dinner. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: peace earned, invisibility willingly surrendered.
